data: That sounds like solid progress on the liveness and cross-epoch pending issues.
The separation of admission-auth from publish state, plus the cumulative frontier handling old pending rows, looks like it cleanly resolves the close deadlock and the permanent-boundary pin.
The 0c1 wrapper distinction (covered published hidden vs.
covered pending visible) is a nice touch for rebase safety.

On the bounded derivation side, the close graph being the authority and the +1 paged observations for the epoch-bound vertices makes sense—especially once they certify ALL admitted rows in the current close.
That keeps the candidate set tight and prevents the lineage from drifting into unbounded 0c1a territory.
The potential edge case you flagged (issued-but-unadmitted suffix rows beyond the graph) is worth watching.
If the paging logic only inspects graph members, a hole in the sequence could still be masked if the later admitted row (which is in the graph) gets seen first.
But 3 being in the graph would still flag the non-dense prefix, so the refusal path should catch it.
The genesis +1 slack is probably just defensive padding.
One thing that still feels a bit fragile is the “exhausted lineage refuses once” rule.
If a genuine room somehow hits the maxEpochVertices limit (unlikely but possible under heavy load or corruption), it would now fail-closed even if the graph itself is well-formed.
Might be worth softening that to a warning + continue, or at least documenting the exact failure mode so operators can distinguish corruption from exhaustion.

On the closure law side, the GREEN wrapper stripping the retirement candidates before calling inspectCreatorTrustAdvance looks like it will preserve existing rejection reasons for unknown kinds, missing cuts, etc.

The extra checks for “exactly one record added at 0→1” and “exactly one replaced at N≥1” are necessary to block adversarial duplicates/missing records, and routing them through TRUST_CLOSURE_INVALID is the right reuse.
current filter-retiring nuance is the only part that still needs a quick sanity check.

If the new wrapper always returns the caller’s proposed (with the retirement candidate included), but the existing stage path already mutates proposed by stripping retiring refs before the inner predicate, you’ll want to make sure the retirement-strip happens *after* the stage filter or that the two are orthogonal.
Otherwise you might end up with a proposed that still contains retiring refs when it reaches the control-plane predicate.
